Subject: Proposal: Indexed Ramp & Staged Refund Framework — Redwood Prepay

Jordan / Taylor,

Thanks again for the time today — attached is the term sheet we discussed with an indexed ramp and a staged refund option that aligns economics to usage growth. High level:

- Structure: 3-year prepay with annual billing windows. Year 1 = 50% prepay, Year 2 = 30% prepay, Year 3 = 20% prepay (applied to committed units).
- Indexed discounts: discounts tiered to year-over-year volume growth (index points embedded in the term sheet; we can swap a fixed discount for an indexed multiplier if you prefer).
- Early termination: proposed decaying refund schedule — full refund within 90 days, 50% between 91–365 days, no refund after 12 months (we call out co-term credits as an alternative).
- Co-terming: we added a section that allows consolidation credits when multiple Redwood lines are co-termed within a 90-day window (formula in section 4).

Attachments: Redwood_Acme_TermSheet_20260907.pdf (term sheet, 3 pages)

Questions for you:
1) Is the staged prepay mix acceptable, or do you want a more front-loaded footprint?
2) Are you open to an escrow-style credit instead of a refund for early termination? That helps preserve unit economics while giving you downside protection.

If this looks directionally right I can get a redline-friendly version over to legal and loop in Marissa for commercial approval.

Best,

Priya —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear breakdown. A few points from procurement/legal that we need clarified/redlined before we can proceed:

1) Co-terming across product lines: We have two separate budget lines — Analytics Suite and Platform API. We need to understand how the consolidation credit applies if one line underperforms. Is it a gross credit or applied only to the co-termed line?

2) Early termination: Our preference is pro-rata refund with a hard stop at 12 months (i.e., no refunds after 12 months) but we would like to see the pro-rata formula explicitly called out. The decaying schedule is close, but procurement wants the math spelled out.

3) Escrow alternative: Procurement is okay with an escrowed credit that vests monthly over 12 months as long as the escrow mechanism is contractual and auditable.

4) Indexed discount: We need an explicit cap on the indexed multiplier (to keep our forecast stable). Please propose a cap and a floor for year-over-year adjustments.

Attached: Acme_Redlines_20260908.docx (redlined term sheet with comments).

We can move quickly once we have a version that our legal can run against.

Jordan —

Appreciate the detailed redlines. Quick internal take and counter-proposal to address your points:

- Co-terming application: the consolidation credit is applied as a gross credit to the co-termed billing account but can be allocated to lines at your direction. We will add language that allows Acme to designate the allocation during reconciliation, with a 90-day window post-co-term to request reallocation.

- Early termination math: agreed we should be explicit. Counter-offer:
  • Refund schedule by days from effective date: 0–90 days = 100% of unused prepay; 91–365 days = 50% of unused prepay; >365 days = 0% refund.
  • Escrow option: instead of cash refunds, we can place refunded value into a dedicated escrow credit balance that vests monthly over the following 12 months and is usable only against Redwood invoices. This escrow balance will be auditable; legal can propose standard language.

- Indexed discount cap/floor: propose cap = +12% year-over-year (attributable to aggressive growth) and floor = -4% (protects against modest decline). We can add a hard cap that requires mutual written consent to exceed.

- Staged ramp: to balance risk we propose a hybrid: Year 1 = 45% prepay, Year 2 = 35% prepay, Year 3 = 20% prepay, and a mid-year true-up at the 12-month anniversary to reconcile actual usage vs forecast. This reduces initial cash while keeping commit signal intact.

I've attached a concise redline summary: Redwood_Response_20260908.txt (summary of changes). If these are acceptable I will loop in Kimberly in legal for a targeted redline and Marissa for final commercial sign-off — hoping to get to a PO within the week.

Best,
Priya
